text:
julia: Heads-up: saw sustained p95/p99 latency on dedicated-pool-eu1 starting ~23:10 UTC. GPUs not fully saturated but host thermals spiked and NIC tx queues ballooned. Any ideas?

marco: which hosts? can you paste a sample allocator line and the node health?

ops-bot: ALERT: host-thermal-throttle detected node=rack7-gpu02 pool=dedicated-pool-eu1 at 2024-08-22T23:12:05Z. auto-ticket INC-6210 created.

julia: alloc sample: `alloc=alloc-d12 node=rack7-gpu02 host=rack7-gw02 tail_p99=380ms egress_q=14 thermal_throttle=1 preempt_count=1 routing=dedicated-egress`

dan: thermal_throttle=1 + egress_q=14 is suspicious. Could be a nightly backup job on the same rack hitting NVMe + NIC. Any cron jobs?

emma: ops-runbook shows nightly-model-sync at 23:00 for staging->eu, uses gw02 as transfer gateway. Might be overlapping with heavy tensorstore writes.

marco: checked `iostat` and `nvme` stats on rack7-gw02: high write latency spikes aligned with tail latency window. NIC `tx_queue` also spiked per `tc -s qdisc`. Looks like IO amplification plus routing fanout to shared egress shim.

julia: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle nightly-model-sync bandwidth 2) move it off rack7 for tonight 3) evacuate low-priority tenants from dedicated-pool-eu1 to warm shared for 2h. Thoughts?

emma: we can patch model-sync to use rsync --bwlimit for tonight (easy), or reschedule. If we evacuate tenants to shared, cost delta is ~12-22% for heavy infer jobs (I can estimate per-tenant).

rachel: oncall note: preempt_count increment suggests our eviction policy is triggering when host thermal crosses threshold. Might want softer backoff to avoid SLO spikes.

dan: short plan: throttle model-sync (emma) now, cordon gw02 for new VIPs (marco), start warm migration for 2 highest-SLO tenants (julia/emma) if metrics not back to normal in 10m.

ops-bot: CHANGE: model-sync bwlimit applied bw=20MB/s for tonight by emma at 2024-08-22T23:18:12Z.

marco: cordon done on rack7-gw02 (conntrack drain initiated). Observed `tx_queue` drop within 90s. Host thermal dropping slowly.

julia: metrics update (1765558940): p99 down to ~42ms from 380ms, preempt count stable. Holding migration off for now.

emma: follow-ups: - add a rack-IO vs egress coupling test in chaos suite - add a scheduler rule to avoid heavy NVMe+egress transfers on racks with dedicated pools during peak windows - add metric host.thermal_eviction_count and alert.

rachel: also propose a small change to eviction policy: add a 30s grace period before preempting active allocs when thermal triggers, to prefer traffic shift first. I'll draft RFC.

julia: agreed. I'll file incident timeline and schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow to land the scheduler rule and adjust eviction grace. Closing thread unless it recurs. :thumbsup:
